claim: Nanometer-scale properties of the extracellular matrix influence many biological processes, including cell motility.
source: Nanometer-scale properties of the extracellular matrix influence many biological processes, including cell motility.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the subsequent experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: Basal keratinocytes collectively migrate on a fibronectin-rich provisional basement membrane to re-epithelialize the injured skin during wound healing.
source: In wound healing, basal keratinocytes collectively migrate on a fibronectin-rich provisional basement membrane to re-epithelialize the injured skin.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The fibronectin receptor integrin α5β1 plays a pivotal role in keratinocyte wound healing.
source: Among other receptors, the fibronectin receptor integrin α5β1 plays a pivotal role in this process.
evidence: This is supported by citations in the introduction and by the experimental design of the study.

claim: Keratinocyte sheets regulate their migration ability at an optimal integrin α5β1 nanospacing.
source: Using a highly specific integrin α5β1 peptidomimetic combined with nanopatterned hydrogels, we show that keratinocyte sheets regulate their migration ability at an optimal integrin α5β1 nanospacing.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1, 4.

claim: The efficiency of keratinocyte migration relies on the effective propagation of stresses within the cell monolayer independent of substrate stiffness.
source: This efficiency relies on the effective propagation of stresses within the cell monolayer independent of substrate stiffness.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from traction force microscopy and monolayer stress microscopy shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Basal keratinocytes collectively migrate to re-epithelialize a wound in the skin as the first step to re-establish tissue integrity.
source: Basal keratinocytes collectively migrate to re-epithelialize a wound in the skin as the first step to re-establish tissue integrity (Bornes et al., 2021; Safferling et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Keratinocytes deposit a provisional basement membrane at the onset of migration that provides the necessary support for adhesion required for cell locomotion.
source: At the onset of migration, keratinocytes deposit a provisional basement membrane that provides the necessary support for adhesion required for cell locomotion (Koivisto et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Fibronectin plays a pivotal role in supporting keratinocyte migration via the adhesion of α5β1 and αvβ1 integrins that are upregulated in re-epithelialization.
source: Among other components of this provisional matrix, fibronectin plays a pivotal role in supporting keratinocyte migration via the adhesion of α5β1 and αvβ1 integrins that are upregulated in re-epithelialization (Cavani et al., 1993; Ffrench-Constant et al., 1989; Grose et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: αvβ1 integrin plays only a minor role in keratinocyte migration.
source: In contrast to αvβ1, which plays only a minor role in migration, α5β1 is required for efficient re-epithelialization, partially through the regulation of cellular traction forces (Schiller et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: α5β1 integrin is required for efficient re-epithelialization, partially through the regulation of cellular traction forces.
source: In contrast to αvβ1, which plays only a minor role in migration, α5β1 is required for efficient re-epithelialization, partially through the regulation of cellular traction forces (Schiller et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In epithelial collective migration, each cell needs to coordinate cell-matrix traction forces with cell-cell stresses in order to propagate directed migratory cues to surrounding neighbours.
source: In epithelial collective migration, each cell needs to coordinate cell-matrix traction forces with cell-cell stresses in order to propagate directed migratory cues to surrounding neighbours (Das et al., 2015; Ladoux and Mège, 2017; Tambe et al., 2011; Vedula et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nanometer-scale properties of the ECM strongly influence cell motility, in particular at the single-cell level.
source: Over the past two decades, it has become clear that nanometer-scale properties of the ECM strongly influence cell motility, in particular at the single-cell level (Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2006; Oria et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Integrin lateral nanospacing plays a critical role in controlling single-cell spreading, migration speed, and persistence.
source: Previous work from our lab has highlighted the critical role of integrin lateral nanospacing in controlling single-cell spreading, migration speed, and persistence (Cavalcanti‐Adam et al., 2008; Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work from the authors' lab.

claim: Lateral adhesion spacing has been shown to regulate intracellular force generation in a manner consistent with the molecular clutch model.
source: Additionally, lateral adhesion spacing has been shown to regulate intracellular force generation in a manner consistent with the molecular clutch model (Oria et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The α5β1 integrin-specific peptidomimetic has a high binding affinity for α5β1 integrin (IC50 = 1.5 nM).
source: This specific peptide has a high binding affinity for α5β1 integrin (IC50 = 1.5 nM), but orders of magnitude lower affinity for the other RGD-recognizing integrins, including αv-containing isoforms (Kapp et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The α5β1 integrin-specific peptidomimetic has orders of magnitude lower affinity for other RGD-recognizing integrins, including αv-containing isoforms, compared to α5β1.
source: This specific peptide has a high binding affinity for α5β1 integrin (IC50 = 1.5 nM), but orders of magnitude lower affinity for the other RGD-recognizing integrins, including αv-containing isoforms (Kapp et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Keratinocytes require an optimal integrin α5β1 spacing in order to efficiently coordinate their collective movement independent from ECM stiffness.
source: We were able to show that keratinocytes require an optimal integrin α5β1 spacing in order to efficiently coordinate their collective movement independent from ECM stiffness.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data in Figures 1, 3, 4.

claim: Gold nanopatterns on glass surfaces were fabricated via block-copolymer micelle nanolithography (BCMN).
source: To investigate the role of integrin α5β1 in regulating keratinocyte collective migration, we fabricated gold nanopatterns on glass surfaces via block-copolymer micelle nanolithography (BCMN).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: BCMN allows for the precise modulation of ligand density at the nanometer level.
source: BCMN allows for the precise modulation of ligand density at the nanometer level.
evidence: This describes a property of the BCMN technique used in the study.

claim: The nanopatterns were covalently transferred onto polyacrylamide (PAA) hydrogels of ~23 kPa stiffness.
source: The nanopatterns were covalently transferred onto polyacrylamide (PAA) hydrogels of ~23 kPa stiffness (approximately the stiffness of freshly wounded skin) (Arnold et al., 2004; Goffin et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental method and is supported by citations.

claim: 23 kPa is approximately the stiffness of freshly wounded skin.
source: The nanopatterns were covalently transferred onto polyacrylamide (PAA) hydrogels of ~23 kPa stiffness (approximately the stiffness of freshly wounded skin) (Arnold et al., 2004; Goffin et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PAA hydrogels are protein-repellent.
source: The use of PAA hydrogels as culture substrate allows us to provide relevant substrate rigidity to cells and systematically control surface adhesion biochemistry due to the protein-repellent nature of PAA.
evidence: This is a known property of PAA hydrogels.

claim: Cells will only interact at nanoparticle sites where highly specific integrin α5β1 peptidomimetics are linked.
source: Therefore, cells will only interact at nanoparticle sites, where highly specific integrin α5β1 peptidomimetics are linked, thereby allowing cell-surface adhesion via integrin α5β1 in a precisely controlled manner (Mas‐Moruno et al., 2016; Rechenmacher et al., 2013; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Three discrete inter-ligand distances were used: 35, 50, and 70 nm.
source: In continuity with previous studies indicating cell-ligand length scale relevance for focal adhesion formation and cell motility, we modulated ligand density using three discrete inter-ligand distances: 35, 50, and 70 nm (Cavalcanti‐Adam et al., 2008; Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Keratinocytes exhibit the highest migration speed (~20 µm/hr) on 50 nm inter-ligand spacing compared to slower speeds (~10 µm/hr) on 35 and 70 nm.
source: Quantifying cell sheet migration speed over culture time revealed a differential migration efficiency on the three conditions, with the highest speed observed at 50 nm (~20 µm/hr) vs. slower speeds at 35 and 70 nm (~10 µm/hr) (Figure 1C and E, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and E.

claim: Human epidermis-derived keratinocytes (hKC) and primary human epidermal keratinocytes (nHEK) also show higher migration efficiency at 50 nm inter-ligand distance.
source: The speed quantification confirmed the higher migration efficiency at 50 nm inter-ligand distance (Figure 1F and G), suggesting this is a universal characteristic of keratinocytes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The higher migration efficiency at 50 nm inter-ligand distance is a universal characteristic of keratinocytes.
source: The speed quantification confirmed the higher migration efficiency at 50 nm inter-ligand distance (Figure 1F and G), suggesting this is a universal characteristic of keratinocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the consistency of results across different keratinocyte types.

claim: Keratinocytes migrating on 50 nm inter-ligand spacing most efficiently coordinate their movements, with an average correlation which extended over ~20 cells (~400 µm).
source: This revealed that keratinocytes migrating on 50 nm inter-ligand spacing most efficiently coordinate their movements, with an average correlation which extended over ~20 cells (~400 µm) (Figure 1D and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and F.

claim: Keratinocytes on both 35 and 70 nm inter-ligand spacing were less able to coordinate their movements, only propagating their movements across a few cells (~200 µm).
source: In contrast, keratinocytes on both 35 and 70 nm inter-ligand spacing were less able to coordinate their movements, only propagating their movements across a few cells (~200 µm) (Figure 1D and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and F.

claim: The density of integrin-ligand interactions alters cell spreading and migratory persistence through the regulation of focal adhesion maturation and dynamics in fibroblasts.
source: The density of integrin-ligand interactions alters cell spreading and migratory persistence through the regulation of focal adhesion maturation and dynamics in fibroblasts (Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2007; Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cells exhibited the highest ability to remodel their focal adhesions when migrating on 50 nm-spaced α5β1 ligands, resulting in the fastest turnover, or lowest lifetime.
source: Cells exhibited the highest ability to remodel their focal adhesions when migrating on 50 nm-spaced α5β1 ligands, resulting in the fastest turnover, or lowest lifetime.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: On 35 and 70 nm inter-ligand spacing, focal adhesions exhibited longer lifetimes and therefore slower remodelling.
source: In contrast, on 35 and 70 nm inter-ligand spacing, focal adhesions exhibited longer lifetimes and therefore slower remodelling (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The average focal adhesion area is smallest in cells on 50 nm compared to 35 or 70 nm inter-ligand spacing.
source: This is supported by the quantified average focal adhesions area, which is the smallest in cells on 50 nm compared to 35 or 70 nm inter-ligand spacing (Figure 2C), as well as focal adhesion length, where we observe the longest adhesions on 70 nm interparticle spacing (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The longest focal adhesions are observed on 70 nm interparticle spacing.
source: This is supported by the quantified average focal adhesions area, which is the smallest in cells on 50 nm compared to 35 or 70 nm inter-ligand spacing (Figure 2C), as well as focal adhesion length, where we observe the longest adhesions on 70 nm interparticle spacing (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cells showed the largest surface contact area and density of focal adhesion at 35 nm which both decrease with increasing interparticle spacing.
source: Cells showed the largest surface contact area and density of focal adhesion at 35 nm which both decrease with increasing interparticle spacing in agreement with the previous reports in similar conditions of single cells (Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B and citations.

claim: During wound healing, basal keratinocytes also interact with their provisional basement membrane using αv-containing integrin isoforms.
source: Integrin α5β1 is not the sole ligand involved in keratinocyte migration. During wound healing, basal keratinocytes also interact with their provisional basement membrane using αv-containing integrin isoforms.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: c(RGDfK) peptide allows for cell adhesion through a broader range of integrins, including αvβ1 and αvβ6.
source: c(RGDfK) allows for cell adhesion through a broader range of integrins, including αvβ1 and αvβ6, which are expressed by basal keratinocytes in the wound (Cavani et al., 1993; Kapp et al., 2017; Koivisto et al., 2014; Sixt et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: αvβ1 and αvβ6 are expressed by basal keratinocytes in the wound.
source: c(RGDfK) allows for cell adhesion through a broader range of integrins, including αvβ1 and αvβ6, which are expressed by basal keratinocytes in the wound (Cavani et al., 1993; Kapp et al., 2017; Koivisto et al., 2014; Sixt et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: c(RGDfK) has lower affinity for α5β1 integrin (IC50 = 200 nM) compared to αv-containing isoforms.
source: While c(RGDfK) still allows for α5β1 interaction, the affinity for this integrin subtype is lower compared to αv-containing isoforms (IC50 = 200 nM) (Kapp et al., 2017; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: On c(RGDfK), keratinocytes exhibit faster migration on 35 nm inter-ligand spacing (vs. 50 nm on α5β1-presenting substrates).
source: Interestingly, on c(RGDfK), keratinocytes exhibit faster migration on 35 nm inter-ligand spacing (vs. 50 nm on α5β1-presenting substrates), and correlation length does not change with receptor densities, which we showed to be biphasic for α5β1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B, C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: On c(RGDfK), correlation length does not change with receptor densities.
source: Interestingly, on c(RGDfK), keratinocytes exhibit faster migration on 35 nm inter-ligand spacing (vs. 50 nm on α5β1-presenting substrates), and correlation length does not change with receptor densities, which we showed to be biphasic for α5β1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B, C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B, C.

claim: There exists a specific optimal integrin α5β1 density that promotes faster focal adhesion dynamics and more efficient keratinocyte coordination, thereby leading to the most effective re-epithelialization process.
source: All together, these data reveal the existence of a specific optimal integrin α5β1 density that promotes faster focal adhesion dynamics and more efficient keratinocyte coordination, thereby leading to the most effective re-epithelialization process.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by the experimental data presented in the Results section.

claim: Epithelial cells coordinate their movements as intercellular stress polarization increases, leading to collective cell migration through mechanotransductive processes.
source: Epithelial cells coordinate their movements as intercellular stress polarization increases, leading to collective cell migration through mechanotransductive processes (Das et al., 2015; Tambe et al., 2011; Trepat and Fredberg, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Integrin nano-presentation in single cells has been shown to regulate not only the persistence of migration but also traction force generation.
source: Integrin nano-presentation in single cells has been shown to regulate not only the persistence of migration but also traction force generation (Cavalcanti-Adam et al., 2007; Oria et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: There is a significant increase in monolayer tractions with decreasing integrin α5β1 ligand density.
source: Surprisingly, this revealed a significant increase in monolayer tractions with decreasing integrin α5β1 ligand density (Figure 3B and C), which did not follow the optimum migratory behaviour (velocity, correlation length) that we observed on 50 nm inter-ligand spacing (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: The distance of stress propagation within the monolayer is crucial for collective cell migration.
source: We previously showed that the distance of stress propagation within the monolayer is crucial for collective cell migration, and that this is related to the levels of actomyosin contraction in individual cells (Das et al., 2015; Vishwakarma et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work from the authors.

claim: The spatial correlation length of the stress vectors was the largest on 50 nm inter-ligand distance (C(r) ~ 200 µm) vs. on 35 or 70 nm (C(r) ~ 50 µm).
source: While the comparison of the absolute values of stress was in line with the traction forces, the spatial correlation length of the stress vectors was the largest on 50 nm inter-ligand distance (C(r) ~ 200 µm) vs. on 35 or 70 nm (C(r) ~ 50 µm) (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: On c(RGDfK)-functionalized substrates, there is no difference between the force correlation length on the three inter-ligand densities.
source: To understand if this stress correlation length relationship was specific to α5β1 integrin, we performed MSM on c(RGDfK)-functionalized substrates. The results show no difference between the force correlation length on the three inter-ligand densities, underlining the specific role of α5β1 in controlling the length of force propagation in keratinocyte monolayers (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The monolayer force correlation length was in line with the velocity correlation length in migrating keratinocyte sheets.
source: In conclusion, the monolayer force correlation length was in line with the velocity correlation length in migrating keratinocyte sheets, suggesting that keratinocytes have an optimum integrin α5β1 density that best dictates the direction of intercellular stresses, and thereby the extent of force propagation in the monolayer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing force and velocity correlation lengths.

claim: Keratinocytes have an optimum integrin α5β1 density that best dictates the direction of intercellular stresses, and thereby the extent of force propagation in the monolayer.
source: In conclusion, the monolayer force correlation length was in line with the velocity correlation length in migrating keratinocyte sheets, suggesting that keratinocytes have an optimum integrin α5β1 density that best dictates the direction of intercellular stresses, and thereby the extent of force propagation in the monolayer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Collective cell migration is affected by substrate rigidity, with stiffer substrates generally enhancing migration efficiency.
source: It has been shown both in vivo and in vitro that collective cell migration is affected by substrate rigidity, with stiffer substrates generally enhancing migration efficiency (Balcioglu et al., 2020; Barriga et al., 2018; Ng et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Focal adhesion lifetime and the stability of its components increase with increasing substrate stiffness and traction forces.
source: Furthermore, it has been observed that focal adhesions lifetime and the stability of its components increase with increasing substrate stiffness and traction forces (Fusco et al., 2017; del et al., 2009; Trichet et al., 2012; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Migration and MSM experiments were performed within an in vivo-relevant range of tissue stiffness on PAA hydrogels of 11, 23, 55, and 90 kPa.
source: Migration and MSM experiments were performed within an in vivo-relevant range of tissue stiffness, that is, on PAA hydrogels of 11, 23, 55, and 90 kPa (Goffin et al., 2006) at the three inter-ligand spacings (35, 50, and 70 nm).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is supported by citation.

claim: Keratinocytes were not able to form cohesive monolayers on the softer (<11 kPa) or stiffer (>90 kPa) nanopatterned surfaces, regardless of spacing.
source: Unlike on protein-coated surfaces (Vishwakarma et al., 2018), keratinocytes were not able to form cohesive monolayers on the softer (<11 kPa) or stiffer (>90 kPa) nanopatterned surfaces, regardless of spacing.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments.

claim: Higher substrate rigidity induced higher migration speed.
source: When comparing stiffness alone, higher substrate rigidity induced higher migration speed, as previously reported by others (Balcioglu et al., 2020; Ng et al., 2012; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and citations.

claim: For each stiffness, cell sheet migratory speed was always more efficient when integrin α5β1 ligand lateral spacing was 50 nm vs. 35 or 70 nm.
source: Interestingly, we observed for each stiffness that cell sheet migratory speed was always more efficient when integrin α5β1 ligand lateral spacing was 50 nm vs. 35 or 70 nm (11 kPa: ~5 µm/hr at 50 nm vs. < ~3 µm/hr at 35 and 70 nm; 23 kPa: ~17 µm/hr vs. < ~9 µm/hr; 55 kPa: ~15 µm/hr vs. < ~10 µm/hr; 90 kPa: ~14 µm/hr vs. < ~9 µm/hr) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The correlation of velocity vectors confirmed a greater ability of keratinocytes to coordinate migration on the 50 nm inter-ligand spaced substrates across different stiffnesses.
source: The correlation of velocity vectors also confirmed a greater ability of keratinocytes to coordinate migration on the 50 nm inter-ligand spaced substrates (11 kPa: ~300 µm vs. ~200 µm; 23 kPa: ~ 400 µm vs. < ~ 200 µm; 55 kPa: ~400 µm vs. ~200 µm; 90 kPa: ~ 350 µm vs. < ~190 µm) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The extent of force propagation within the monolayers confirms the higher force-propagation capability when integrin α5β1 ligand has a lateral spacing of 50 nm.
source: The extent of force propagation within the monolayers also confirms the higher force-propagation capability when integrin α5β1 ligand has a lateral spacing of 50 nm (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MSM could not be carried out reliably on the stiff 90 kPa hydrogels due to limited bead movement caused by the specific surface functionalization, resulting in a high signal-to-noise ratio of the bead displacements.
source: MSM could not be carried out reliably on the stiff 90 kPa hydrogels due to limited bead movement caused by the specific surface functionalization, resulting in a high signal-to-noise ratio of the bead displacements.
evidence: This explains a limitation in the experimental methodology.

claim: In epithelial sheets, the actin cytoskeleton physically connects cell-ECM adhesion structures with cell-cell adhesions.
source: In epithelial sheets, the actin cytoskeleton physically connects cell-ECM adhesion structures with cell-cell adhesions (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Adherens junctions are responsible for maintaining the intercellular force continuum via E-cadherin-based homophilic interactions.
source: Between the latter, adherens junctions are responsible for maintaining the intercellular force continuum via E-cadherin-based homophilic interactions (Bazellières et al., 2015; Li et al., 2012; Ng et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The mechanical continuum provided by adherens junctions is crucial for coordinating collective migration by regulating intercellular pulling forces necessary for mechanotransduction pathways upstream of cell polarization.
source: This mechanical continuum is crucial for coordinating collective migration by regulating intercellular pulling forces necessary for mechanotransduction pathways upstream of cell polarization (Das et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Outside of the optimal 50 nm inter-ligand spacing of α5β1 peptide, single keratinocytes would move counterproductively, thereby inhibiting monolayer motion.
source: We hypothesized that outside of the optimal 50 nm inter-ligand spacing of α5β1 peptide we observed, single keratinocytes would move counterproductively, thereby inhibiting monolayer motion.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their observations.

claim: When E-cadherin was inhibited, keratinocyte migration was enhanced on both 35 and 70 nm inter-ligand spacing vs. 50 nm.
source: When E-cadherin was inhibited, keratinocyte migration was enhanced on both 35 and 70 nm inter-ligand spacing vs. 50 nm, as indicated by the distance of migration over culture time (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: When quantifying the change in sheet speed after inhibition of E-cadherin vs. untreated cells, migration speed was reduced on 50 nm vs. enhanced on 35 and 70 nm.
source: Furthermore, when quantifying the change in sheet speed, Δv, after inhibition of E-cadherin vs. untreated cells, we observed migration speed was reduced on 50 nm vs. enhanced on 35 and 70 nm (Figure 5B, Video 5), indicating that the previously observed migration efficiency on 50 nm requires precise coordination between cell-cell and cell-ECM structures.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The migration efficiency on 50 nm requires precise coordination between cell-cell and cell-ECM structures.
source: Furthermore, when quantifying the change in sheet speed, Δv, after inhibition of E-cadherin vs. untreated cells, we observed migration speed was reduced on 50 nm vs. enhanced on 35 and 70 nm (Figure 5B, Video 5), indicating that the previously observed migration efficiency on 50 nm requires precise coordination between cell-cell and cell-ECM structures.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the E-cadherin inhibition experiments.

claim: Integrin α5β1 lateral spacing plays a vital role in regulating keratinocyte collective migration.
source: All together, these data indicate a vital role of integrin α5β1 lateral spacing in regulating keratinocyte collective migration.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by all the experimental data presented.

claim: The optimal 50 nm lateral spacing outweighs the effect of substrate rigidity.
source: The optimal 50 nm lateral spacing outweighs the effect of substrate rigidity, as well as regulates E-cadherin-mediated transmission of intercellular forces.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments comparing different stiffnesses.

claim: The optimal 50 nm lateral spacing regulates E-cadherin-mediated transmission of intercellular forces.
source: The optimal 50 nm lateral spacing outweighs the effect of substrate rigidity, as well as regulates E-cadherin-mediated transmission of intercellular forces.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the E-cadherin inhibition experiments.

claim: Ligand nanospacing is integral to collective migration in keratinocytes, even outweighing the effects of substrate stiffness.
source: We show here that ligand nanospacing is integral to collective migration in keratinocytes, even outweighing the effects of substrate stiffness.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the Discussion section, supported by all experimental data.

claim: 50 nm inter-ligand distance is optimal for integrin α5β1, whereby collective cell migratory speed and coordination were enhanced.
source: Specifically, we found that 50 nm inter-ligand distance is optimal for integrin α5β1, whereby collective cell migratory speed (Figure 1C and E) and coordination were enhanced.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and E.

claim: At 50 nm inter-ligand distance, integrin α5β1 promotes the largest velocity correlation within the monolayer vs. at lower or higher ligand spacing (~400 µm on 50 nm vs. ~200 µm on 35 or 70 nm).
source: At this distance, integrin α5β1 promotes the largest velocity correlation within the monolayer vs. at lower or higher ligand spacing (~400 µm on 50 nm vs. ~200 µm on 35 or 70 nm), indicating that cell movements are transmitted up to 20 cell lengths within the sheet.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Cell movements are transmitted up to 20 cell lengths within the sheet at 50 nm inter-ligand spacing.
source: At this distance, integrin α5β1 promotes the largest velocity correlation within the monolayer vs. at lower or higher ligand spacing (~400 µm on 50 nm vs. ~200 µm on 35 or 70 nm), indicating that cell movements are transmitted up to 20 cell lengths within the sheet.
evidence: This is inferred from the velocity correlation length data.

claim: Keratinocytes on 50 nm ligand spacing exhibited the most dynamic focal adhesions, with short lifetimes of ~14 min vs. ~16 min on 35 or 70 nm.
source: Consistent with enhanced migration, keratinocytes on this ligand spacing also exhibited the most dynamic focal adhesions, with short lifetimes of ~14 min vs. ~16 min on 35 or 70 nm (Figures 1D, F, 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1D, F, 2.

claim: The ideal inter-ligand spacing is not dependent on the absolute traction forces generated on the surface, but rather by the correlation length of stress vectors in the monolayer.
source: Quantification of the monolayer stress distribution revelated that this ideal inter-ligand spacing is not dependent on the absolute traction forces generated on the surface, but rather by the correlation length of stress vectors in the monolayer (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Keratinocytes exhibited enhanced migratory behaviour (faster and larger velocity and stress correlation lengths) at 50 nm spacing regardless of substrate stiffness on hydrogels of varying Young's moduli (11–90 kPa).
source: This was also confirmed on hydrogels of varying Young's moduli (11–90 kPa), with keratinocytes exhibiting enhanced migratory behaviour (faster and larger velocity and stress correlation lengths) at 50 nm spacing regardless of substrate stiffness (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Higher substrate rigidity is generally known to induce greater cellular traction forces, resulting in faster epithelial sheet migration.
source: This was particularly interesting because higher substrate rigidity is generally known to induce greater cellular traction forces, resulting in faster epithelial sheet migration (Balcioglu et al., 2020; Ng et al., 2012; Sunyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Each epithelial cell within a monolayer migrates in the direction of the maximal normal stress in a phenomenon called plithotaxis.
source: Each epithelial cell within a monolayer migrates in the direction of the maximal normal stress in a phenomenon called plithotaxis (Tambe et al., 2011; Trepat and Fredberg, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Adherens junctions, which are connected to the actin cytoskeleton, are required for intercellular force transmission in cell collectives.
source: In cell collectives, adherens junctions, which are connected to the actin cytoskeleton, are required for intercellular force transmission (Bazellières et al., 2015; Ng et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The actin cytoskeleton is connected to the ECM, which explains why disrupted keratinocyte migration was observed on 50 nm integrin α5β1 ligand lateral spacing when E-cadherin interactions were inhibited.
source: As the actin cytoskeleton is also connected to the ECM, this explains why we observed disrupted keratinocyte migration on 50 nm integrin α5β1 ligand lateral spacing when E-cadherin interactions were inhibited by addition of DECMA-1 antibody (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results and established knowledge.

claim: At higher and lower ligand spacing, keratinocytes were able to migrate faster when intercellular force transmission was disturbed.
source: In contrast, at higher and lower ligand spacing, keratinocytes were able to migrate faster when we disturbed intercellular force transmission (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Outside of the optimal integrin α5β1 inter-receptor spacing of 50 nm, uncorrelated intercellular stresses slow keratinocyte sheet migration and result in inefficient collective movement.
source: Therefore, we can conclude that outside of the optimal integrin α5β1 inter-receptor spacing of 50 nm, uncorrelated intercellular stresses slow keratinocyte sheet migration and result in inefficient collective movement (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: Integrin α5β1 regulates the generation of traction forces upon adhesion, whereas αv-class integrins mediate ECM rigidity sensing in single cells.
source: It has previously been shown in single cells that integrin α5β1 regulates the generation of traction forces upon adhesion, whereas αv-class integrins mediate ECM rigidity sensing (Schiller et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Faster collective migration is observed with increasing substrate stiffness.
source: While we do observe faster collective migration with increasing substrate stiffness, as has been previously reported (Figure 4A; Balcioglu et al., 2020; Ng et al., 2012; Sunyer et al., 2016), α5β1 inter-receptor spacing outweighs stiffness effects alone.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and citations.

claim: α5β1 inter-receptor spacing outweighs stiffness effects alone.
source: While we do observe faster collective migration with increasing substrate stiffness, as has been previously reported (Figure 4A; Balcioglu et al., 2020; Ng et al., 2012; Sunyer et al., 2016), α5β1 inter-receptor spacing outweighs stiffness effects alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing stiffness and spacing effects.

claim: Higher substrate rigidity causes higher traction forces at the sheet edge at the outset of migration, thereby transmitting higher net stress to the cell followers, ultimately resulting in more efficient collective migration.
source: Indeed, higher substrate rigidity causes higher traction forces at the sheet edge at the outset of migration (removal of PDMS stencil), thereby transmitting higher net stress to the cell followers, ultimately resulting in more efficient collective migration (Sunyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 50 nm lateral spacing of integrin α5β1 is required for efficient force transmission independent from the net force exerted on the cells.
source: This validates our data that 50 nm lateral spacing of integrin α5β1 is required for efficient force transmission independent from the net force exerted on the cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The severe phenotype acquired by murine animal models genetically lacking α5 or β1 integrin subunits has prevented deep understanding into the roles specific integrin subtypes and organization play in wound healing.
source: The severe phenotype acquired by murine animal models genetically lacking α5 or β1 integrin subunits has prevented our deep understanding into the roles specific integrin subtypes and organization play in wound healing (Raghavan et al., 2000; Yang et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The bottom-up approach systematically identified the importance of integrin α5β1 density in coordinating force propagation within keratinocyte monolayers.
source: With our bottom-up approach, we systematically identified the importance of integrin α5β1 density in coordinating force propagation within keratinocyte monolayers.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's contribution.

claim: An integrin subtype-specific arrangement may be present in specific biological contexts that function through mechanosensitive pathways mediated by focal adhesions.
source: How this inter-ligand optimal spacing can be understood in the in vivo context still requires further exploration, but our findings suggest that an integrin subtype-specific arrangement may be present in specific biological contexts that function through mechanosensitive pathways mediated by focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the findings of the study.

claim: Cell monolayer density and proliferation rate were comparable among all three inter-ligand distances.
source: Cell monolayer density and their proliferation rate were comparable among all three inter-ligand distances (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.
